Key Research Thinking Patterns: Uncertainty-aware, decision-driven ML: integrate calibrated uncertainty with practical thresholds to guide real-world lab decisions
Domain-informed ML: fuse physics/chemistry/engineering knowledge with data-driven models (structure-aware representations, physics constraints)
Robustness to distribution shifts and temporal labeling changes: use self-supervised pathways and temporal splits to enhance generalization
Scalability and interpretability: emphasize feature selection, robust baselines, and interpretable pathways (e.g., chemical reasoning, periodic-table embeddings)
Data efficiency through augmentation and hybrid modeling: combine real and synthetic data with surrogate models to accelerate design

Summary Description: Mike Banad is a cross-disciplinary ML researcher known for integrating advanced machine learning with domain-rich scientific and engineering problems. His work spans materials informatics, photonics design, energy systems, IoT-enabled healthcare, and neuroimaging. A central thread is the development of uncertainty-aware, data-efficient, and interpretable ML pipelines that couple physics-informed representations with modern generative and discriminative models. Notable contributions include the SyntheFormer framework for structure-aware synthesizability prediction under extreme class imbalance, uncertainty calibration for practical lab decision-making, and a Philippine-style blend of generative augmentation (WGAN-GP) with surrogate predictors (XGBoost) for inverse design in photonics. His research emphasizes robust deployment, reproducibility, and the bridging of theory with lab-ready, decision-support tools across materials science, photonics, smart grids, and healthcare.
